disputed: The court found the process illegal but did not strike the report's scientific content from the record ('lets their science stand,' per C&EN). The authors and DOE defend the report as a legitimate review of uncertainties. Mainstream scientific bodies broadly reject its conclusions.

items: The court found the group operated in secret and gave 'substantive policy advice and recommendations' without the transparency and balanced membership the law requires. (EDF (https://www.edf.org/media/court-rules-trump-administrations-secret-climate-working-group-violated-federal-law); C&EN (https://cen.acs.org/policy/litigation/doe-climate-working-group-illegal/104/web/2026/02))

EPA's Endangerment Finding repeal proposal cited the report 22 times. Internal DOE documents show the report was created to justify administration policy. (EDF (https://www.edf.org/media/court-rules-trump-administrations-secret-climate-working-group-violated-federal-law); UCS (https://blog.ucs.org/science-blogger/internal-doe-documents-confirm-climate-report-was-created-to-justify-administration-policy/))

EPA finalized the repeal on Feb 12, 2026, removing the legal basis for federal greenhouse-gas limits on cars, power plants and oil fields. (See the 'Environmental deregulation under EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin' item.)
sections.label: Documentation

summary: Wright's Energy Department assembled five hand-picked climate contrarians to write a report questioning mainstream climate science. EPA cited it 22 times in proposing to repeal the Endangerment Finding. A federal court ruled on Jan 30, 2026 that the group violated the Federal Advisory Committee Act.
title: DOE's secret 'Climate Working Group' built the case for repealing the Endangerment Finding
